headline: TikTok Reviewer's Viral Love Letter Sells Out Indie Comic Series Overnight
meta_description: A TikTok creator with 40K followers discovered a Nigerian-heritage comic at Anime NYC and posted about it. His million-liked video drove 25,000 new followers t…
summary_short: One enthusiastic TikTok post about an indie comic series inspired by Yoruba culture brought overnight success to its creator, selling out physical copies within hours.
body:
A TikTok content creator known for stopping at overlooked comic book booths has inadvertently launched an indie comic series into the spotlight. @slow_comics, who has built a following of 40,000 by championing underrated creators at conventions, discovered artist Dare's work at Anime NYC—a sumptuously-illustrated series called Ori: Holder of the Heads, rooted in Yoruba African culture. The story follows characters investigating why ancestors have begun attacking people, accompanied by a complementary comic called Etch that can be read in two directions, each offering a different perspective on a dispute between two creatures.

When @slow_comics posted about the discovery, expressing ecstatic enthusiasm for the art style, African cloth patterns, and innovative storytelling, the response was staggering. The video received one million likes and redirected 25,000 new followers to Dare's creator account. The surge in attention meant all outstanding copies at the convention sold out immediately, forcing Dare to call his brother Joshua to drive physical stock from Pennsylvania to New York—which also sold out completely.

What makes this story remarkable isn't just the numbers, but what it reveals about social media's potential. Rather than a polished marketing campaign, a genuine recommendation from one creator to thousands sparked real economic opportunity for an independent artist. Dare subsequently posted a follow-up video thanking the community and announcing that preorders for Ori and Etch would reopen, demonstrating how organic enthusiasm can transform careers. The comics are scheduled to appear at the Small Press Expo in Bethesda, Maryland on September 12-13, followed by the Uhuru Book Fair in Philadelphia. In an age of endless digital noise, one person's authentic passion proved more powerful than any algorithm.
quick_facts: TikTok creator @slow_comics has 40,000 followers on his platform
His viral post about Ori: Holder of the Heads reached 1 million likes
The post generated 25,000 new followers for artist Dare (@Oridipe)
All physical comic copies sold out at Anime NYC and online within hours
Comics feature Yoruba Nigerian heritage and include bidirectional comic Etch
